summary: Egon Wellesz studied at the University of Vienna (~1904–1908). He later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1913–1938) and as a lecturer at the University of Oxford (1943).

Eido Shimano, working in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa (Ryutaku-ji, 1954), and attended the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and held posts at New York Zendo Shobo-ji, Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji, and Shogen Junior College.

Eiichi Imoto worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1949–1953), he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1996) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1996–2001).

Eiichi Makino, active in philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Kyushu University, Shiraume Gakuen Junior College, Chuo University, and Tohoku University.
Eiichi Otani, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Toyo University. As of 2026, he is attested as dean and professor (学部長・教授) at Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Eiichi Yamaguchi, working in Indology and philosophy, was a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and later served there as a research assistant (attested 1990–1991).
Eiju Fukushima works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. By 2026, he is attested as faculty at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.
Eikan Taki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a member of Taisho University and, as of 2006, was a lecturer (講師) at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.
Eiki Hoshino, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Taisho University. He held an appointment at Taisho University as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director.
Eiko Okukaze, a Buddhist studies scholar, was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010). Okukaze is attested as a commissioned researcher (受託研究員) at Koyasan University in 2026.

Eileen M. Dimes studied at the University of London (B.A., 1932). Specializing in Indology, she worked in the library at SOAS University of London (1945) and succeeded Alfred Master as Assistant Keeper for Modern Indian languages at the India Office Records (1959).

Eileen Power, a historian, studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1907–1910) and the University of Paris (~1910–1911) after attending Oxford High School. She held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

Eilhard Mitscherlich studied at Heidelberg, Paris (under A.-L. Chézy and A.-I. Silvestre de Sacy), Göttingen, Berlin, and Stockholm. He held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (1822) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1821–1863), working in Iranian and Central Asian studies and chemistry.

Eino Wälikangas studied at the University of Helsinki (M.A. 1914) under doctoral supervisor J. N. Reuter. Working in Indology and linguistics, he held a post teaching Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki.

Eisaku Okada, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and served as a JSPS DC fellow (2014) and part-time lecturer (2015). At Koyasan University, he was a commissioned researcher (2014) and special-appointment lecturer (2026).
Eisei Kojima was a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1976) and president of Doho University (attested 1976).
Eishu Miyazaki, active in Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied at Rissho University under Gyoo Kageyama. He later held posts at Rissho University and Minobusan University.
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson (attested 1998).

Eivind Kahrs, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studied under Nils Simonsson. He held a post at Queens' College (attested 2010) and serves as a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eiyin Yasuda, active in Buddhist studies, studied at Ryukoku University and was a disciple under Gyōin Hashimoto.
